overall: As of 08:50 ET, temperatures have reached 75.0°F with an extremely high dewpoint of 73.0°F — near saturation — suggesting the atmosphere is already laden with moisture ahead of incoming storms. The day's running max was recorded as early as 08:11 ET, and with negative acceleration (-0.99°F/hr²) and flat 30-minute velocity, warming momentum is already fading. A Flood Watch is in effect through July 7, and increasing cloud cover from showers and afternoon thunderstorms (50% PoP today) is expected to cap daytime heating significantly.
forecast_obs_notes: There is a notable split between raw NWP guidance (GFS 88.4°F, ECMWF 90.9°F, HRRR 91.7°F, NBM 88.1°F) and the NWS official forecast of 83°F — a gap of roughly 5-9 degrees. max_temp_prediction: The most likely daily high is in the 82-83F range, consistent with both the NWS official forecast (~83°F) and the META model's top even bucket (82-83F at 36%). For the active Kalshi even-bucket market, the D1_NOW ensemble highlights 84-85F as the top bucket at 30.8%, but the higher-fidelity META model downgrades that outcome significantly. Given the early warming plateau, near-saturated boundary layer, Flood Watch cloud cover, and negative heating acceleration, confidence is moderate-to-good that the high stays at or just below 83°F; a pop above 84°F would require storms to hold off longer than forecast.
